hobson-s-choice-a-lancashire-comedy-in-f: Harold Brighouse's beloved Lancashire comedy centers on Henry Hobson, a blustering Salford bootmaker who refuses to marry off his daughters. His eldest, Maggie, takes matters into her own hands: she marries Will Mossop, Hobson's best craftsman, and the pair open a rival shop across the street. First staged in 1915, the play's battle of wits between father and daughter still delights audiences.
the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-1: Beyond the emperors, Suetonius also wrote brief lives of Rome's great poets — and these surviving fragments are a treasure. Virgil, Horace, Lucan, and others appear in quick, gossipy sketches full of literary anecdote. For anyone who loves classical literature, these pages offer rare glimpses of the men behind the verses.
the-bores-a-comedy-in-three-acts: Molière's Les Fâcheux lampoons the bores every age knows — the hunters, gamblers, and pedants who devour a busy man's day. Written in a fortnight for a royal entertainment, the comedy became an instant Paris hit. Its gallery of time-wasters remains painfully, hilariously recognizable.
the-emancipation-of-massachusetts: Brooks Adams shows how Massachusetts cast off the yoke of its Puritan priests and won soul-liberty. Out of court books and old records he builds the tale of the harried dissenters and their triumph. Bold and well-pleaded, it upset many a cozy New England myth.
vautrin-a-drama-in-five-acts: Balzac brings his most famous criminal — Vautrin, the escaped convict who haunts the Human Comedy — to the stage in this drama. The master manipulator schemes through Parisian society with diabolical charm. Banned in its day for its daring, the play shows Balzac's genius in theatrical form.
belinda-an-april-folly-in-three-acts: A. A. Milne — years before Winnie-the-Pooh — wrote this sparkling three-act comedy of an April folly that turns a respectable household upside down. Witty dialogue, romantic confusion, and Milne's light, deft touch fill an evening's entertainment. The play shows the future children's author as a sophisticated West End playwright at the height of his early powers.
a-girl-among-the-anarchists: Isabel Meredith's novel takes a brave girl among the anarchists of London — the secret plots, the high ideals, the very real dangers of the movement. Written from inside knowledge, it thrills while it makes readers think. A rare window onto a shadowy, passionate world.
men-women-and-boats: Stephen Crane gathers his sea stories — including the immortal Open Boat — tales of men, women, and boats against the ocean's might. His impressionistic genius shines in every line. Among the finest short stories in English. The Open Boat alone would secure his fame; the companion pieces confirm it.
mr-pim-passes-by-a-comedy-in-three-acts: A. A. Milne's charming comedy turns on Mr. Pim, whose passing remark upends a respectable household. Mistaken identities and romantic tangles follow in delightful confusion. Milne the playwright at his lightest and best. One man's casual lie sets three acts of delicious confusion in motion.
on-nothing-kindred-subjects: Hilaire Belloc discourses on nothing and kindred subjects — essays on trifles that open into great truths about inns, lanes, and the human lot. His robust humor and rolling periods never fail to please. Belloc's paradoxical wisdom at its most playful.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acceptants: This 1913 reference piece on the Acceptants — those who accepted the bull Unigenitus against Jansenism. Pierre Fournet tells their side. France's church split over the quarrel. Orthodoxy's party in a bitter fight. The quarrel outlived both its parties. Rome's thunder settled the matter at last.
